proxy_language: Proto-Khoe-Kwadi / Khoe (Khoekhoe, Nama) with Juu (!Xun, Ju|'hoan) click-language morphology as secondary reference; both used as a loose areal proxy for Later Stone Age southern Africa
proxy_rationale: The Robberg industry (c. 22,000-12,000 BP; Robberg Peninsula, Plettenberg Bay, and sites across southern Africa) is a purely archaeological Later Stone Age microlithic bladelet tradition with no linguistic record. Its makers were ancestral hunter-gatherers of the region, and the click-bearing Khoisan languages (Juu, Tuu, Khoe-Kwadi) are the only living languages whose speakers descend, at least partly, from such populations. The link is very weak: Khoisan is not a demonstrated single family, the time depth is far beyond the comparative method, and Khoe-Kwadi probably arrived from the north only c. 2,000 years ago. Names should therefore be modeled on documented Khoisan phonology (clicks, glottalised and aspirated consonants, C(C)V(N) syllables) and presented as a flavored approximation, never as 'Robberg language'.
phonology: Modeled on Nama/Khoekhoegowab (Haacke, Hagman) with Ju|'hoan features. Consonants: plain stops p t k, aspirated/affricated kh, ts, tsh (Nama ts, kx), voiced b d g, nasals m n, fricatives s h x (velar), liquid r. Clicks in four accompaniments of Nama: dental |, alveolar-palatal !, lateral ||, bilabial/palatal-ish (rare) with series: plain, aspirated, nasal, glottalised. Vowels: a e i o u, with nasalised vowels and (in Nama) four tones (high, mid, low, rising); Ju|'hoan adds pharyngealised, breathy and murmured vowels, and has many click accompaniments (>40 click phonemes). Glottal stop is phonemic and common word-medially.
phonotactics: Typical root shapes CV, CVV, CVCV, CVN; Nama roots are mostly bimoraic (CVCV) and words end in a vowel or in -m, -n, -b, -s, -ts, -ra, -ge as gender/number suffixes. Syllable onset is a single consonant or click (clusters are only click+k-type or C+glottal). Medial consonants are limited to a subset (b, d, g, m, n, r, plain clicks). Codas are essentially absent in Ju|'hoan and Nama roots except nasals. Hiatus and long vowels (VV) occur. Glottal stop (') is written between vowels or after consonants.
orthography: Practical Latin transliteration after the Khoekhoegowab orthography and Ju|'hoan standard orthography: click symbols | (dental), ! (alveolar), || (lateral) and, in broader transcription, \u2260 (palatal); click accompaniments written after the click (|h aspirated, |' glottalised, n| nasal as 'n|' or 'g|' for voiced, etc.). For Latin-script auditing, ASCII approximation recommended: clicks rendered as the letters q (dental/alveolar-type), x (lateral/dental-type) and c (dental-type) as in Zulu/Xhosa-style southern African Bantu orthographies, plus ' for glottal/ejective release; tones unmarked. Diacritics (acute on vowels) optional for tone; nasalised vowels may be written with a following n.
morphology: Nama is agglutinating with nominal suffixes for gender (-b masculine, -s feminine, -i common/neuter singular), number (-gu/-kx'a masc/fem plural in Nama: -gu, -ku, -di, -n, -ra), and postpositions. Pronouns cliticise to the first constituent. Verbs take a suffixal system of derivations (reciprocal, causative, applicative). Ju|'hoan is largely isolating with noun-class concord via pronoun-like agreement and prefixes (class markers such as ju- 'person', n!ang 'person-' variants). Reduplication is productive for plural/intensity and plurality in several Khoisan languages.
compounding: Nama and Ju|'hoan form compounds head-final: modifier + head noun (e.g. Nama |gaub 'spoor' + ...). Genitive/possessive relations are expressed by juxtaposition with possessor first (possessor-possessed) in Juu and by a possessive postposition/linker in Khoekhoe. 'X of Y' = Y + X (possessor first); 'Y-maker' = verb stem + nominal agentive/gender suffix (e.g. -b 'masc agent') or noun + verb compound. Descriptive names often use animal/plant terms plus colour or size terms. Names of places commonly end in a locative element (Nama -s 'place of/at', e.g. !Gaingu).
noun_phrase_order: Head-final in Khoekhoe: modifier + noun (adjective precedes noun, possessor precedes possessed, demonstrative precedes noun). Juu: possessor + possessed; adjectives follow the noun in Ju|'hoan with concord; numerals follow. For game purposes use modifier-first, head noun last.

attested_roots.gloss: water (Ju|'hoan chu / Nama !ao-variants; approximate rendering of the root 'water')
bird (Khoisan roots with ts'-; cf. Nama tsii)
person, Khoe people (Nama khoe 'person', Khoekhoe 'people of people')

worked_examples.name: Khamsa'ae
worked_examples.gloss: khams (sun) + a (linker) + 'ae (sit/dwell: place where the sun dwells)

notes: No word may be identical to a Modern Irish, Scottish Gaelic or Manx word. Robberg has no linguistic record: this is a speculative Khoisan-flavored approximation and the glosses of several roots are approximate renderings of Khoekhoe/Juu forms rather than verified lexical entries. Click letters are approximated with Latin q/x/c and the apostrophe for Latin-script audits; do not use ! or | in output names.
